To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the blockchain is secure under a more general class of external attacks, namely long delay attacks with delay \(\ge 1/ np\); (b) the blockchain is also secure in the honest but curious miner model, i.e. when the external adversary has access to all the information of the honest miners; and (c) the blockchain can tolerate inconsistency in the ledger.
“In a blockchain with \(n\) miners and \(p\) the mining difficulty the blockchain is secure if the delay in message propagation is at most \(\Delta \le 1/np \) in an asynchronous network.”

the blockchain is provably secure against long delay attack in an asynchronous network with \(\varSigma \ge 1/p\) (in the honest miner setting), where \(\varSigma =\max \{\varDelta,1/n\}\) is the total latency of the network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the security of the blockchain protocol in an asynchronous network against external attacks.
the security of the Bitcoin protocol in the face of an external adversary that can maliciously delay messages by an amount that grows with the number of miners.
the security analysis of the blockchain against long delay attacks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the honest miner model, a blockchain is secure in a network where messages can be delayed by any constant factor, as long as there is no adversarial delay.
the blockchain is indeed secure under the honest miner setting, and that the security holds for any delay \(\varDelta <1/2p\), where p is the mining hardness and n is the number of miners.
the blockchain is provably secure in the asynchronous setting as long as the delay is less than the expected time to solve a block.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the asynchronous network, if the miners are honest, the blockchain is secure as long as the delay of external attack is bounded by \(\varDelta < 1/np.\)
in an asynchronous network, the security of the blockchain can be guaranteed as long as honest nodes are sufficiently many and the mining hardness is sufficiently high.
the security of the blockchain against malicious delay attacks is determined by the ratio \(\varDelta /np\).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the security of the blockchain is robust against external attacks.
the blockchain is surprisingly robust against external attacks in the asynchronous setting.
the security of the blockchain can be significantly strengthened by allowing a limited number of blocks with incorrect transactions to be included in the chain.
